audit.whatIsWrong: Three fabricated mechanics shipped: 'Akshan's passive camouflage triggers off nearby minion deaths' (camouflage is Going Rogue (W), an activated 18s spell, not a passive off minion deaths); 'Comeback Time' as his ultimate (his ult is Comeuppance; the revive is Going Rogue and only fires when he kills a Scoundrel — the enemy who killed his ally); and 'auto-attack resets' (Dirty Fighting fires an extra reduced-damage attack and shields on every third hit — it is not a reset). Dirty Fighting's shield, the single most important thing about bursting him, was never mentioned. 'Fox Fire' was also flagged as a suspect name.
audit.why: Riot text: Dirty Fighting shields on every third hit from attacks or abilities; Going Rogue is the camouflage and revive; Comeuppance locks on from 2500 and stores bullets scaling with missing health. Charm 'instantly stops movement abilities', which applies to Heroic Swing.

edits.before: Akshan's passive camouflage triggers off nearby minion deaths, so early waves he vanishes mid-trade and punishes your Orb of Deception with free autos you can't return.
edits.after: Dirty Fighting shields him on every third hit from an attack or ability, so early waves he eats your Orb of Deception, absorbs the return, and autos back while you wait on the 7s recast.

edits.before: Comeback Time can revive a dead ally the instant you kill them, so any all-in you win can be undone unless you finish the fight fast or your team follows up before his passive triggers.
edits.after: Going Rogue revives his fallen allies only if he kills a Scoundrel — the enemy who killed them — so once you take that kill you are the mark, and Comeuppance from 2500 range is how he collects.

edits.before: Once you finish Shadowflame/Luden's your burst clears his low HP pool in one Orb-Charm-Fox Fire combo before he can land three autos back, flipping every skirmish your way.
edits.after: Once you finish Shadowflame/Luden's your burst clears his low HP pool in one Orb-Charm-fox-fire combo before Dirty Fighting stacks a third hit, flipping every skirmish your way.

edits.before: Level 1-2 belongs to Akshan — his camouflage plus auto-attack resets let him punish your immobile early poke, and he can freely disengage into brush before you can Charm him, so you're stuck playing passive and losing CS.
edits.after: Level 1-2 belongs to Akshan — Avengerang damages going out and back and extends its range off each hit, and Dirty Fighting shields his every third hit, so you cannot win the poke war and should farm what you can safely reach.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 stay roughly even as your Charm range starts threatening his auto-reset pattern, but it's still a Skill-check phase since a well-timed camo engage from him can still punish a bad position, while level 6 tips clearly to you — Spirit Rush lets you dodge his skillshots and land a full combo he can't revive through fast enough.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 stay roughly even: Charm at 975 range outreaches Avengerang's 850 and instantly stops Heroic Swing mid-flight, but his 18s swing still punishes a bad position, while level 6 tips clearly to you — Spirit Rush's three dashes break Comeuppance's firing line and let you combo before his shield restacks.

edits.before: Auto-reset combo through camo whenever minions die nearby
edits.after: Land a third Dirty Fighting hit to shield through your burst

edits.before: Bank ult charge from his passive to threaten flank picks

notes: This matchup carried three outright fabrications — camouflage 'triggering off nearby minion deaths', an ultimate called 'Comeback Time', and Akshan having auto-attack resets. All three are replaced with Riot's actual kit. The revive belongs to Going Rogue (W) and is conditional on killing a Scoundrel, which is a real and under-used piece of advice for an Ahri who just took a kill. Charm stopping Heroic Swing mid-swing follows from Riot's 'instantly stopping movement abilities' line but I could not verify frame-level behaviour, so it is phrased as stopping the swing rather than promising a guaranteed dismount. tradeGood/tradeBad remain fully templated and duplicated into breakdown.trading and report[3].t; nothing in Akshan's kit gave me a same-length replacement I could ground, so they are left.
